correctness.rationale: The p(v)>0 quadratic makes H=x^2/2+K(v) a proper first integral, with compact smooth positive-energy ovals. Counting both x signs gives the exact velocity density proportional to p(v)^(-1)*(1-2K/A^2)^(-1/2) on the two turning points, and equal sign-branch weights. Under nu, K(V) has a square-root integrable density at zero and exponentially decaying large-energy tail; splitting the moving endpoint region proves w_A=1+K/A^2+O_L1(A^-4) and yields the displayed sharp total-variation coefficient after normalization. Symmetric alpha=0 angular coordinates give the Clausen identity. The marked position-face variable converges by tightness and local uniformity. Independent direct Clausen integral evaluation recovered 0.3230659472194505 for beta=1.
